rationale: A comprehensive multicenter study and systematic literature synthesis by Iruzubieta et al. (2024; 50 total patients) rigorously evaluated the global cohort of patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants and established an exact split into two distinct mutational cohorts rather than a phenotypic continuum: 26/50 (52%) individuals harbored biallelic loss-of-function (LoF)/null variants presenting with childhood-onset spasticity, neurodevelopmental delay, early stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss mimicking periventricular leukomalacia; whereas 24/50 (48%) individuals harbored biallelic cysteine-altering missense variants presenting with adult-onset CADASIL-spectrum arteriopathy (subcortical lacunar infarcts, dementia, and deep white matter lesions sparing significant volume loss). Independent family and cohort reports (Stellingwerff et al. 2022, Tasharrofi et al. 2024, Al 2023) confirm that recessive null/LoF variants cause severe, early-onset neurodevelopmental/vascular leukoencephalopathy distinct from typical CADASIL.

evidence.text: In a systematic multi-center and literature analysis of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants, 26 patients harbored biallelic loss-of-function variants resulting in pediatric-onset neurodevelopmental delay, spasticity, childhood stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss, whereas 24 patients had biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants resulting in adult-onset CADASIL spectrum phenotype with strokes and dementia without significant volume loss.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Our systematic analyses verified distinct genotype-phenotype correlations for the two types of biallelic variants in NOTCH3. Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: Detailed clinical records of three patients from two families with biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants revealed symptom presentation at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, recurrent strokes, microbleeds, microcalcifications, and sparing of anterior temporal lobes, confirming a distinct childhood-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: The patients presented at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, or both. The disease course was characterized by cognitive impairment and variably recurrent strokes, migraine attacks, and seizures... Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

evidence.text: A homozygous frameshift null variant (c.2984delC) produced livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions, confirming recessive inheritance distinct from CADASIL dominant gain-of-function.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: WES of the proband identified a novel homozygous NOTCH3 null variant (c.2984delC)... The findings of this study suggest an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern in this early-onset leukoencephalopathy, in contrast to CADASIL's dominant gain-of-function mechanism; which is a clear example of genotype-phenotype correlation.

evidence.text: Two siblings with homozygous nonsense variants (Arg735Ter) presented with severe congenital phenotypes including eye misalignment, visual impairment, epilepsy, global developmental delay, and pyramidal signs, demonstrating that biallelic null variants cause a phenotype far more severe and early-onset than dominantly inherited cysteine-altering CADASIL.

source.title: Autosomal recessive NOTCH3-related leukodystrophy in two siblings and review of the literature
source.quote: These patients presented with a severe congenital phenotype, including eye misalignment, visual impairment, epilepsy, global developmental delay, and subsequent development of pyramidal signs. Biallelic nonsense variants were discovered in both the cases (NM_000435.3:c.2203 C > T (p. [Arg735Ter]).

evidence.text: A patient harboring a cysteine-altering variant (p.Cys1146Ser) in trans with a frameshift null variant (p.Cys1024Valfs248) presented in his mid-thirties with progressive gait disturbance, dysphagia, slurred speech, lacunar infarcts, and microbleeds, illustrating that mixed cysteine/LoF compound heterozygotes follow the adult-onset CADASIL spectrum rather than pediatric recessive leukoencephalopathy.

source.title: An in trans NOTCH3 loss-of-function variant modifies disease severity in CADASIL: A family-based study
source.quote: The proband, carrying p.Cys1146Ser and p.Cys1024Valfs248 in trans, developed progressive gait disturbance, dysphagia, and slurred speech beginning in his mid-thirties. Brain MRI demonstrated extensive white matter hyperintensities, multiple lacunar infarcts, and numerous cerebral microbleeds.

new_directions.question_text: How do compound heterozygous combinations of one cysteine-altering allele and one null/LoF allele in trans clinically and neuropathologically differ from homozygous cysteine-altering CADASIL cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: While homozygous LoF causes pediatric-onset recessive leukoencephalopathy and homozygous cysteine missense causes classic CADASIL, trans heterozygous combinations of LoF and cysteine variants (as in Lan et al.) appear to manifest as mid-adulthood CADASIL, indicating that a single cysteine-altering allele dictates the adult-onset vascular proteopathy phenotype.

new_directions.question_text: What specific vascular smooth muscle cell and pericyte signaling pathways are ablated in biallelic NOTCH3 null leukoencephalopathy that lead to early periatrial volume loss without anterior temporal pole involvement?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying why anterior temporal pole hyperintensities (classic for CADASIL) are spared in recessive NOTCH3 LoF patients while periventricular leukomalacia-like periatrial volume loss is pronounced will reveal the distinct developmental vascular roles of NOTCH3 signaling versus NOTCH3 extracellular domain aggregation.
